audiences.executive: Ransomware on one laptop should stay on one laptop: seen in minutes, isolated in one click, any time of day.
audiences.technical: An agent on every device, prevention on everywhere, exclusions reviewed, isolation in seconds, and someone answering a critical alert at night.
audiences.financial: Fewer machines rebuilt and fewer hours lost to an attack that spreads; one agent instead of several overlapping tools.

people: Security operations, who answer the alerts
The desktop and server teams, who deploy the agent
Branch and contractor managers, for the devices nobody counts

objections.says: We already have antivirus on every machine.
objections.clarify: How many devices have no agent at all, servers, branches and contractors included?
objections.answer: Coverage is what counts: find the devices without an agent first, then make sure prevention is on where it is installed.
objections.prove: Compare the device inventory with the agents reporting, and list the machines missing.

objections.says: Prevention mode will break our applications.
objections.clarify: Which applications broke last time, and which groups are still in detect-only mode because of them?
objections.answer: Turn prevention on group by group, with exclusions that are narrow, reviewed and owned.
objections.prove: Switch one detect-only group to prevention for two weeks, and record what was blocked and what broke.

objections.says: Nobody is watching the alerts at night.
objections.clarify: When the last critical alert fired out of hours, when was it answered?
objections.answer: Isolation can happen on its own for the clearest cases, and a service can answer the rest out of hours.
objections.prove: Trigger a test alert at night, and time it from the alert to the machine isolated.
